application_guidance.input_pattern: Fixed finite sum with globally convex smooth components, repeatable exact indexed gradient access and the specified zero-table SAG update.
read_original_when: A Proof requires independently verified computer-assisted steps or the mu=0/small-n boundary treatment.
Changing initialization, sampling, step size, Oracle, output or component assumptions.
Using a centered-gradient initialization or practical implementation variant outside this selected scope.
sensitive_conditions: The component smoothness bound L, rather than merely a smoothness bound for g, controls alpha.
General convex and strongly convex branches have different outputs.
sigma^2 is the average squared component-gradient norm at an optimum and may remain positive.
Random uniform sampling cannot be replaced by cyclic order using this statement.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Expectation over Algorithm randomness on each fixed admissible instance, for every integer k>=1.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: All constants are explicit in the displayed bounds. C_init depends on initial objective gap, distance to the chosen optimum, L,n and sigma^2; sigma^2 need not be zero and is not a tuning input.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact indexed component gradients; independent uniform component selection with replacement.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Expected objective gap at bar x^k for the general convex branch; at x^k for the strongly convex branch. These output choices are part of the guarantee.
complexity_scope.regime: Global smooth convex finite sums with an attained minimum; linear branch additionally requires global strong convexity of g.
complexity_scope.resource: k component-gradient queries, k index draws, O(np) dense table storage, O(p) dense vector arithmetic per update plus gradient computation, and O(p) average accumulation per update when needed. Initialization requires no gradient calls but does require table allocation/initialization.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper bound for the specific zero-table SAG trajectory; no coverage of unrestricted algorithms or lower-bound assertion.

content.intended_use: Provide the selected Algorithm's expected objective-gap upper bound; not a lower bound or guarantee for arbitrary Oracle algorithms.

proofs.locator: Appendix B.1–B.8, pp.34–48; selected zero-table initialization in B.8.1, p.47
map: B.1, pp.34–36: introduce stacked gradient-table/iterate state theta, optimum state theta*, filtration generated by sampled indices and the conditional first moments. Lemma 1 states the conditional quadratic-form recursion, citing the 2012 paper for its derivation. Lemma 2 gives the inverse for the two orthogonal block projectors and includes its multiplication proof.
B.2, p.37: use a Lyapunov function consisting of 2h[g(x+d e^T y)-g(x*)] plus a block quadratic form, with A=a1 ee^T+a2 I, B=b e and C=cI. Seek conditional contraction and domination of objective gap.

B.3, pp.37–41: combine Lemma 1, convexity/strong convexity and smoothness bounds (12)–(13); Table 3 groups terms. Maximize the table-error quadratic using Lemma 2, then bound component gradient differences using convex smoothness to reduce drift to scalar coefficient constraints.

B.4–B.5, pp.42–43: minimize the quadratic over table state to obtain objective-gap domination constraints, combine them with drift constraints 1–9, and select explicit coefficients. The choice includes alpha=1/(16L), delta=min{1/(8n),mu/(16L)}, gamma=1 and C3=1/(32n). n=1 is treated by the source as gradient descent; the displayed coefficient analysis assumes n>1.

B.6, pp.43–46: normalize L=1 and split at mu=2/n. The well-conditioned case reduces to univariate positivity in 1/n. The ill-conditioned case uses x=1/n and y=n mu/2, monotonicity/endpoints, and separate n in {2,3,4} checks. Embedded Matlab code checks polynomial roots and midpoint signs; the external full script is referenced by the source but was not acquired or executed here.

B.7, pp.46–47: use objective-gap domination and conditional drift <=-(1/(32n))<x^(k-1)-x*,grad g(x^(k-1))>. For positive delta iterate contraction. For mu=0 telescope the drift and apply Jensen to the average of x^0,...,x^(k-1).
B.8.1, p.47: substitute y^0=0 into the selected Lyapunov function, use sum_i grad f_i(x*)=0, and bound its initial value by C_init. Combine with B.7 to recover the selected Theorem 1 bounds.

assumptions: Every f_i is convex and differentiable on all of R^p, and ||grad f_i(x)-grad f_i(z)||<=L||x-z|| for every x,z in R^p and every i.
g attains its minimum at x*; functions and data are deterministic and fixed.
Exact component-gradient queries, zero table initialization, independent uniform sampling with replacement and constant alpha=1/(16L).
Only for the linear-rate conclusion: g(x)-(mu/2)||x||^2 is convex for some mu>0; individual f_i need not be strongly convex.
statement.conclusion: E[g(bar x^k)]-g(x*) <= (32n/k) C_init. If g is additionally mu-strongly convex, E[g(x^k)]-g(x*) <= (1-min{mu/(16L),1/(8n)})^k C_init. This record selects only the zero-table branch of Theorem 1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n,p be positive integers, f_i:R^p->R, and g(x)=(1/n)sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x). Use Euclidean norms. Choose x* in argmin g and x^0 in R^p. Define sigma^2=(1/n)sum_i ||grad f_i(x*)||^2 and C_init=g(x^0)-g(x*)+(4L/n)||x^0-x*||^2+sigma^2/(16L). Set y_i^0=0. For t>=1 choose i_t uniformly and independently, refresh y_{i_t}^t=grad f_{i_t}(x^(t-1)), retain the other entries, and set x^t=x^(t-1)-(1/(16Ln))sum_i y_i^t. Define bar x^k=(1/k)sum_{t=0}^{k-1}x^t.
statement.parameter_domains: n,p in positive integers; L>0; k>=1 integer. For the strongly convex branch 0<mu<=L. No bounded-domain or bounded-gradient assumption is imposed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such finite-sum instance, every initial point x^0 and chosen minimizer x*, and every integer k>=1, the stated inequalities hold. Expectations are solely over i_1,...,i_k, with the fixed instance and initialization held fixed.
